messages:
alex: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8140 — quick heads up. Microbatch scheduling tweak in this PR shows a p95 latency bump (~+15%) on longseq profiles and ~+200MB p95 memory on our 1k-token run. Bench artifacts uploaded. Can I get reviews/2nds and a decision on merge timing? Prefer to either canary tomorrow or hold until we validate. cc @maya @sourav

bench-bot: Auto-bench report for PR #8140:
p50: 85ms -> 86ms (+1.2%)
p95: 212ms -> 244ms (+15%)
throughput: 720 -> 698 (-3.1%)
mem p95: 5.2GB -> 5.4GB (+200MB)
Artifacts: https://bench.redwood.com/artifacts/8140 (csv + flamegraphs)
Compare: https://bench.redwood.com/compare/8139...8140

maya: Can you drop the raw flamegraph here? Quick glance makes me suspicious of a kernel change rather than allocator, fyi. :thinking_face:

sourav: I can look in a bit. Need perf-runner logs + the exact bench command you used. Did this touch kv-sharding or quant kernels?

alex: Logs + flamegraph in S3: s3://redwood-bench/8140/ (local-run + runner stdout). Bench command we used:
```
./bench --profile=longseq --runs=10 --model=redwood-v2-large --batch=8
```
This PR only touches microbatch scheduling path (allocator handoff). No kv-shard changes. Quant kernel v2 in use.

jen: Given p95 moves and mem delta, I'd prefer to canary first on a low-traffic region. I can schedule a canary for tomorrow morning if we hold merge until then.

liam: +1 on holding. +200MB could push some of our small GPU instances over the pack threshold. If we merge now we risk a rollout OOM. Prefer canary unless we get a clear sign it's safe. :warning:

sourav: I'll run a targeted microbench locally tonight (same flags) and post results. If it's tail-only and not changing median we might accept with rollback hooks.

alex: Thanks — I've added a quick rollback plan to the PR description and linked the canary checklist. If no objections by 18:00 UTC we'll either merge with canary-disabled and immediate rollback enabled, or wait based on feedback.

bench-bot: Canary slots open at 09:00 PST tomorrow. Use deploy-bot to claim a slot; bench artifacts will be collected automatically.

jen: Claiming the 09:00 PST canary slot now via deploy-bot. Also, please add a short note in guards.md about the expected mem delta so oncall is aware.

jen: moving PR -> merge-hold queue :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: Uploaded the perf-runner logs from my repro to s3://redwood-bench/8140/local-run-logs.txt

sourav: Uploaded local microbench results and a flamegraph: https://bench.redwood.com/artifacts/8140/local-flame.svg — preliminary looks: scheduler wait increased ~3-4% CPU, p95 locally +10%, mem pretty stable.

liam: :thumbsup: If canary passes I'll do post-canary approval. @maya can you take the kernel selection line in the PR diff?

maya: Yep — I'll review kernel selection tonight and post any concerns.

jen: Holding merge until canary completes and logs look good. Thanks everyone.

alex: Appreciate the quick responses — I'll update the PR with the canary flag and exact rollback steps now.
